To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HIV infection is associated with an increased prevalence of HPV infection, HPV-associated disease, and HPV-associated neoplasia in both women and in men.
HIV infection is a risk factor for HPV infection, that HIV infection is an important risk factor for HPV-associated neoplasias, and that HPV infection is common in persons infected with HIV.

understanding the natural history of HPV infection in HIV-infected individuals and the role of HIV infection in the pathogenesis of HPV-induced neoplasia in both women and in men.

HIV infection is associated with an increased risk of HPV infection, and the risk increases in proportion to the severity of HIV-induced immunosuppression; that the risk of HPV-associated cervical and anal dysplasia is increased in women and men with immunosuppression due to HIV; and that the risk of progression of HPV-associated dysplasia to invasive disease is increased in HIV-seropositive individuals.
